definitionEn: to give someone an official honour, degree or right, or to give an advantage
senseNote: Выбрано значение «присваивать, предоставлять» (confer a degree on someone); значение «совещаться» (confer with colleagues) не отрабатывается.
situation: A university, state or other authority officially gives someone a title, degree or right, or something brings an advantage.

examples.text: The university will [[confer]] an honorary degree on the author at next month's ceremony.
Citizenship [[confers]] certain rights, such as the right to vote and to hold a passport.
Speaking several languages can [[confer]] a real advantage in the job market.

texts: The title was [[conferred]] on him for services to medicine.
Membership of the club [[conferred]] a certain status on the whole family.
The degrees were [[conferred]] at a small ceremony in the college chapel.

badCollocation.noteRu: Confer не берёт два дополнения подряд: не confer someone a title, а confer a title on someone.

collocationTask.prompt: ___ an honorary degree on the singer
collocationTask.explanationRu: Почётную степень присваивают — confer a degree on someone (или bestow). Appoint — назначать на должность, donate — жертвовать, assign — поручать.

nuance.text: In the past, owning land [[conferred]] enormous social status on a family.
nuance.explanationRu: Confer — официально дать статус, право или преимущество (confer on). Award — вручить приз, премию или оценку (award to); статус не вручают как награду.

reverse.text: She was [[awarded]] first prize in the national poetry competition.
reverse.explanationRu: Приз на конкурсе вручают — award. Confer — торжественно присвоить звание, степень или право, а не приз.

fixIt.text: Last year the academy [[assigned]] an honorary title on the retired professor.
fixIt.explanationRu: Assign — поручить задание или назначить номер. Звание присваивают — confer a title on someone.

reply.context: A friend messages: "My old university is giving my grandmother an honorary doctorate!"
options: Wow! Will she confer with them about it first?
Kindly convey my felicitations upon the conferring of said doctorate.
Amazing! When do they confer it? I'd love to be at the ceremony.
reply.explanationRu: Confer a doctorate — присвоить почётную степень. В первом ответе confer with понято как «совещаться», второй звучит как старинное официальное письмо.

rewrite.original: The university gave her an honorary degree in 2019.
rewrite.explanationRu: Пассив с предлогом on: a degree was conferred on her.

definitionEn: a formal statement in which someone admits that they have committed a crime
senseNote: Выбрано значение «признание вины» (sign a confession); личное «признание» (I have a confession to make) и «исповедь» не отрабатываются.
situation: Police or a court get a statement from a suspect in which he or she admits committing the crime.

examples.text: The suspect signed a [[confession]] after twelve hours of questioning.
The judge ruled that his [[confession]] could not be used because police had threatened him.
The detective series ends when the butler makes a full [[confession]] to the theft.

texts: Police say the [[confession]] matches the evidence found at the scene.
She later withdrew her [[confession]], claiming she had been confused and exhausted.
Without a [[confession]], the case against him is surprisingly weak.

badCollocation.noteRu: Признание делают — make a confession (или sign, give a full confession); do здесь не подходит.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Признаться — make a confession (или give, sign a confession). Do, take и say с confession не сочетаются.

nuance.text: After ten hours of questioning, the suspect finally made a full [[confession]].
nuance.explanationRu: Русское «признание» бывает разным: признание вины — confession, признание заслуг — recognition. На допросе делают confession.

reverse.text: The scientist finally received [[recognition]] for her work on the vaccine.
reverse.explanationRu: Признание заслуг, известность — recognition. Confession — признание вины, к научной работе не подходит.

fixIt.text: The court heard that his [[acknowledgement]] had been obtained under pressure.
fixIt.explanationRu: Признание вины в суде или полиции — confession. Acknowledgement — подтверждение получения или благодарность.

wordFormation.text: After three days, the police finally got a [[confession]] from the driver.

reply.context: Watching a crime drama, your friend says: "I can't believe the neighbour did it all along!"
options: Me neither. And his confession in the last scene was so calm and cold.
Me neither. The police even gave him a confession for being so helpful.
Indeed, his confession constitutes a legally admissible statement of guilt.
reply.explanationRu: Confession — признание вины, первый ответ естественный. Во втором confession ошибочно значит «награда», третий звучит как протокол, а не разговор у телевизора.

definitionEn: the way in which the parts of something are arranged or set up
situation: You describe how the parts of a room, vehicle, machine or computer system are arranged or set up.

examples.text: The airline changed the seating [[configuration]] so that each plane can carry twenty more passengers.
Before installing the update, save a copy of your current network [[configuration]].
The two molecules contain the same atoms, but in a different [[configuration]].

texts: The hall can be used in almost any [[configuration]], from rows of chairs to small tables.
Engineers tested a new wing [[configuration]] in the wind tunnel.
The default [[configuration]] works well for most home users.

badCollocation.noteRu: О форме лица, тела или предмета говорят shape. Configuration — расположение частей техники или системы.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Расположение кресел — seating configuration (или seating plan). Construction — строительство, consideration — рассмотрение, confirmation — подтверждение.

nuance.text: The IT team keeps a record of the [[configuration]] of every server in the building.
nuance.explanationRu: Configuration — общее устройство системы: какие части и как они собраны и настроены. Setting — один параметр, который можно менять: яркость, громкость.

reverse.text: Turn up the brightness [[setting]] if the screen looks too dark.
reverse.explanationRu: Отдельный параметр, например яркость, — setting. Configuration — устройство системы целиком.

fixIt.text: Two laptops that look identical may run differently if their hardware [[composition]] is different.
fixIt.explanationRu: Как собран и настроен компьютер — hardware configuration. Composition — химический состав или состав группы людей.

wordFormation.text: Incorrect [[configuration]] is the most common cause of network problems in small offices.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "Why is the meeting room full of round tables today?"
options: They've changed the configuration of the tables, so they're rounder now.
They've changed the configuration for the workshop. It'll be back to rows tomorrow.
The configuration has been modified pursuant to the facilitator's specifications.
reply.explanationRu: Configuration — расстановка мебели в зале, второй ответ естественный. В первом слово понято как форма столов, третий звучит как инструкция, а не ответ коллеге.

definitionEn: to limit an activity or problem to a particular place, group or subject
senseNote: Выбрано значение «ограничивать рамками» (be confined to, confine yourself to); значение «держать взаперти» не отрабатывается.
situation: Something happens only in one place, group or topic, or you deliberately keep it within those limits.

examples.text: The problem is not [[confined]] to big cities; many small towns are struggling too.
Please [[confine]] your questions to the topic of today's talk.
This rare frog is [[confined]] to a single valley in the mountains.

texts: Luckily, the damage was [[confined]] to the kitchen.
His interests are not [[confined]] to football; he also paints.
For centuries, the plant was [[confined]] to a few gardens in Japan.

badCollocation.noteRu: Ограничивать себя в еде — cut down on sugar или limit yourself. Confine yourself to — ограничиться чем-то: confine yourself to two questions.

collocationTask.prompt: The virus was largely ___ to older patients.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Be confined to — ограничиваться чем-то, встречаться только там. Closed, locked и shut — про двери и помещения, а не про рамки явления.

nuance.text: Let's [[confine]] the discussion to the budget and leave staffing until next week.
nuance.explanationRu: Confine — ограничить рамками: confine the discussion to the budget. Confide — доверить тайну: confide in someone. Слова похожи, но значения разные.

reverse.text: She [[confided]] in her sister that she was thinking of leaving her job.
reverse.explanationRu: Поделиться секретом, довериться — confide in someone. Confine значит «ограничить».

fixIt.text: In the past, the disease was [[restrained]] to a few remote villages.
fixIt.explanationRu: Restrain — сдерживать, удерживать силой. «Ограничивалась несколькими деревнями» — was confined to.

rewrite.original: The problem affects only the northern part of the country.
rewrite.frame: The problem ____ the northern part of the country.

definitionEn: a statement or piece of evidence showing that something is definitely true
senseNote: Выбрано значение «подтверждение факта» (official confirmation, confirmation of a theory), а не базовое «подтверждение бронирования».
situation: An official statement, a test or new evidence shows that something people suspected is definitely true.

examples.text: The club has given no official [[confirmation]] that the coach is leaving.
The new data provide strong [[confirmation]] of a theory first proposed in the 1960s.
Her silence was all the [[confirmation]] I needed that something was seriously wrong.

texts: We're still waiting for [[confirmation]] from the lab.
The news came as [[confirmation]] of what everyone had suspected.
Police are seeking [[confirmation]] of the man's identity.

badCollocation.noteRu: Подтверждение дают или получают — give, receive, get confirmation; do здесь не подходит.

collocationTask.prompt: We are still awaiting ___ from the ministry.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Ждать официального подтверждения — await confirmation. Confrontation — столкновение, consolation — утешение, conversation — разговор.

nuance.text: We have received [[confirmation]] that the samples arrived safely at the lab.
nuance.explanationRu: Confirmation — подтверждение, что что-то правда или точно произойдёт. Approval — одобрение, разрешение; то, что образцы доехали, — факт, его подтверждают.

reverse.text: Children under sixteen need their parents' [[approval]] to join the trip.
reverse.explanationRu: Разрешение родителей — approval. Confirmation подтверждает факт, а не даёт разрешение.

fixIt.text: The rumours about the merger received official [[proof]] on Friday morning.
fixIt.explanationRu: Слухи официально подтверждают — receive official confirmation. Proof — доказательство, его не «получают официально».

wordFormation.text: Independent [[confirmation]] of the findings is expected within weeks.

reply.context: A colleague messages: "I heard the office is moving to the city centre. Is that true?"
options: Only if the boss gives her confirmation. She hasn't decided yet.
That's the rumour, but we haven't had any official confirmation yet.
Affirmative. Confirmation of said relocation is pending, as per protocol.
reply.explanationRu: Official confirmation — официальное подтверждение факта. В первом ответе confirmation ошибочно значит «разрешение», третий звучит как военный рапорт.

rewrite.original: Nobody has officially confirmed the date of the concert yet.
rewrite.frame: There has been no ____ of the concert date yet.

definitionEn: to behave or think in the same way as most people in a group or society
senseNote: Выбрано значение «вести себя как все, следовать нормам группы» (pressure to conform); значение «соответствовать стандартам» не отрабатывается.
situation: People change their behaviour, clothes or opinions to match what their group or society expects.

examples.text: Teenagers often feel huge pressure to [[conform]], even when it means hiding who they really are.
At my old firm, anyone who refused to [[conform]] to the long-hours culture was quietly sidelined.
Her paintings never [[conformed]] to the fashions of the time, which is why critics ignored her.

texts: In a small village, there is strong pressure to [[conform]].
Schools should teach children to think, not just to [[conform]].
Some people [[conform]] simply because they are afraid of standing out.

badCollocation.noteRu: Conform всегда с предлогом: conform to (или with) the rules; без предлога — ошибка.

collocationTask.prompt: strong pressure to ___ to social norms
collocationTask.explanationRu: Подстраиваться под нормы — conform to social norms. Obey, follow и respect берут дополнение без to: obey the rules.

nuance.text: He dyed his hair green partly because he refused to [[conform]].
nuance.explanationRu: Conform — вести себя как все, подстраиваться под нормы группы. Obey — выполнять приказ или закон, и ему нужно дополнение: obey the law, obey your parents.

reverse.text: Drivers must [[obey]] the speed limit near schools.
reverse.explanationRu: Соблюдать закон или правило — obey the speed limit. Conform требует to и говорит скорее о социальных нормах.

fixIt.text: People who [[correspond]] to what society expects are rarely criticised.
fixIt.explanationRu: Correspond to — соответствовать (о фактах, данных). Вести себя так, как ждёт общество, — conform to.

wordFormation.text: Critics say the school values [[conformity]] more than creativity.

reply.context: A friend says: "My new company expects everyone to wear a suit, even on Fridays."
options: Will your suit conform? Maybe get it taken in a bit.
Will you conform, or keep wearing jeans and see what happens?
One is obliged to conform to the sartorial expectations of one's employer.
reply.explanationRu: Conform — подстроиться под правила и нормы, второй ответ естественный. В первом conform ошибочно значит «подходить по размеру», третий звучит слишком напыщенно.

definitionEn: to face a difficult problem or situation and start dealing with it
senseNote: Выбрано значение «смело встретить проблему, взяться за неё» (confront a problem, confront your fears); значение «выяснять отношения с кем-то» не отрабатывается.
situation: Instead of avoiding a difficult problem, fear or truth, you face it directly and deal with it.

examples.text: The new government must [[confront]] the housing crisis instead of blaming the previous one.
Therapy helped her [[confront]] her fear of flying after years of avoiding planes.
Sooner or later, the company will have to [[confront]] the fact that its main product is out of date.

texts: Doctors are [[confronted]] with difficult choices every day.
Many small farms are [[confronted]] with rising costs and falling prices.
She finally [[confronted]] the grief she had been avoiding for years.

badCollocation.noteRu: В активе confront без предлога: confront a problem. With нужен только в пассиве: be confronted with a problem.

collocationTask.prompt: Doctors are often ___ with impossible choices.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Столкнуться с трудностью — be confronted (или faced) with. Collide, crash и bump — физическое столкновение машин или предметов.

nuance.text: Instead of running away, she decided to [[confront]] her fear of public speaking.
nuance.explanationRu: Confront — сознательно встретить проблему лицом к лицу. Encounter — случайно столкнуться с чем-то; решить «encounter» свой страх нельзя.

reverse.text: On our walk through the forest, we [[encountered]] a family of deer.
reverse.explanationRu: Случайно встретить кого-то в пути — encounter. Confront — встретить проблему или человека с вызовом, к оленям на прогулке не подходит.

fixIt.text: Sooner or later, every manager has to [[oppose]] the problem of staff burnout.
fixIt.explanationRu: Oppose — выступать против идеи или решения. Смело взяться за проблему — confront a problem.

wordFormation.text: Try to avoid a [[confrontation]] with your manager in front of the whole team.

reply.context: A friend says: "I keep putting off opening my bank statements. I'm scared to see how bad it is."
options: Good idea. Confront it for a few more months and it'll go away by itself.
One must confront one's pecuniary obligations with fortitude.
I get it, but you'll feel better once you confront it. Let's look together.
reply.explanationRu: Confront — смело взглянуть проблеме в лицо, третий ответ естественный. В первом confront ошибочно значит «избегать», второй звучит напыщенно.

rewrite.original: Sooner or later, you have to deal with your problems instead of running away from them.
rewrite.frame: Sooner or later, you have to ____ instead of running away from them.
rewrite.explanationRu: Confront a problem — смело взяться за проблему.

definitionEn: an angry argument or conflict between people or groups who strongly disagree
situation: Two people or groups face each other angrily because they strongly disagree, and a fight or row seems likely.

examples.text: She avoided a [[confrontation]] with her boss by raising the issue calmly in an email.
Police stood between the two groups of fans to prevent a violent [[confrontation]].
Every family dinner turned into a [[confrontation]] about politics, so we stopped meeting.

texts: The minister wants to avoid a [[confrontation]] with the unions.
After months of tension, a [[confrontation]] between the neighbours seemed unavoidable.
The film builds slowly towards a final [[confrontation]] between the two brothers.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Столкновение мнений» — a clash of opinions (или views). Confrontation — открытый конфликт людей или групп.

collocationTask.prompt: The police wanted to avoid a direct ___ with the protesters.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Прямое столкновение — a direct confrontation. Confession — признание вины, consultation — совещание, congregation — прихожане.

nuance.text: Security had to step in when a [[confrontation]] broke out between two passengers at the gate.
nuance.explanationRu: Confrontation — прямое столкновение людей лицом к лицу. Controversy — общественный спор, полемика вокруг решения; у выхода на посадку такой не «вспыхивает».

reverse.text: The decision to cancel the festival caused a lot of [[controversy]] online.
reverse.explanationRu: Бурные споры в обществе и в сети — controversy. Confrontation — стычка конкретных людей или групп лицом к лицу.

fixIt.text: There was a short [[collision]] between two groups of fans outside the stadium.
fixIt.explanationRu: Collision — столкновение машин или предметов. Стычка людей — confrontation.

wordFormation.text: His [[confrontational]] style makes every meeting feel like a battle.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "Should I tell Mark in front of everyone that his report was full of mistakes?"
options: Yes, a confrontation would be a lovely way to thank him.
I'd avoid a public confrontation. Talk to him privately first.
Confrontation is contraindicated; kindly pursue a bilateral dialogue.
reply.explanationRu: Avoid a confrontation — избежать открытого конфликта, второй ответ естественный. В первом confrontation понято как что-то приятное, третий звучит как канцелярский жаргон.

rewrite.original: The two leaders argued angrily in front of the cameras.
rewrite.frame: There was an angry ____ in front of the cameras.
rewrite.explanationRu: A confrontation between — открытое столкновение между кем-то.

definitionEn: to feel pleased with yourself about something you have done well or achieved
senseNote: Выбрано значение congratulate yourself (on something) — гордиться собой, хвалить себя; базовое «поздравлять кого-то» (B1) не отрабатывается.
situation: After a success or a smart decision, you privately feel proud and satisfied with what you did.

examples.text: When it started pouring, we [[congratulated]] ourselves on bringing umbrellas.
The team [[congratulated]] themselves on finishing the project two weeks early, but then the client changed everything.
Don't [[congratulate]] yourself too soon: the hardest part of the course is still ahead.

texts: She quietly [[congratulated]] herself on staying calm during the interview.
The organisers [[congratulated]] themselves on selling every single ticket.
He [[congratulated]] himself on finding such a cheap flat so close to the centre.

collocations: [[congratulate]] ourselves on a job well done

badCollocation.noteRu: По-английски congratulate on, а не with: congratulate yourself on a success.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Гордиться собой, «похвалить себя» за успех — congratulate yourself on something. Greet и welcome — приветствовать, celebrate — праздновать.

nuance.text: After parking perfectly on the first try, he [[congratulated]] himself on his driving.
nuance.explanationRu: Congratulate yourself on — порадоваться конкретному успеху (удачно припарковался). Pride yourself on — постоянно гордиться своим качеством: she prides herself on being punctual.

reverse.text: Our restaurant [[prides]] itself on using only local ingredients.
reverse.explanationRu: Постоянное качество, которым гордятся, — pride yourself on. Congratulate yourself — о радости от конкретного успеха.

fixIt.text: After the exam, I [[greeted]] myself on not panicking once.
fixIt.explanationRu: Greet — приветствовать. Похвалить себя за успех — congratulate yourself on something.

reply.context: A colleague messages: "We've hit our sales target a week early!"
options: Oh no, that's terrible. We should congratulate ourselves on the mistake.
Brilliant! We can definitely congratulate ourselves on that one.
Kindly accept this acknowledgement that self-congratulation is warranted.
reply.explanationRu: Congratulate ourselves on — порадоваться своему успеху, второй ответ естественный. В первом слово связано с ошибкой, третий звучит как нелепая официальная записка.

rewrite.original: I felt very proud of myself for finishing the marathon.
rewrite.explanationRu: Congratulate yourself on something — гордиться собой за что-то.

definitionEn: the people attending a religious service, or the regular members of a church
situation: You talk about the people who come together in a church, mosque or synagogue to worship.

examples.text: The [[congregation]] stood and sang as the bride walked down the aisle.
Over the past twenty years, the church's [[congregation]] has shrunk to fewer than thirty people.
Members of the mosque's [[congregation]] take turns cooking meals for homeless people.

texts: The whole [[congregation]] rose to its feet for the final hymn.
The new vicar greeted each member of the [[congregation]] at the door.
Some of the [[congregation]] had travelled for hours to attend the funeral.

badCollocation.noteRu: Зрители на матче — crowd; congregation — только люди на богослужении.

collocationTask.prompt: The priest turned to address the ___.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Людей на службе в церкви называют congregation. Consultation — совещание, conversation — разговор, concentration — сосредоточенность.

nuance.text: At the end of the service, the priest blessed the [[congregation]].
nuance.explanationRu: Congregation — люди на богослужении, они молятся, а не смотрят шоу. Audience — зрители или слушатели концерта, спектакля, лекции.

reverse.text: The [[audience]] applauded for five minutes after the concert.
reverse.explanationRu: Публика на концерте — audience; congregation — только о прихожанах на службе.

fixIt.text: The [[public]] in the church stood up when the choir began to sing.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Публика» в церкви — congregation. Public — общество в целом, а не люди на службе.

wordFormation.text: Fans began to [[congregate]] outside the stadium hours before the match.
